carbon_policy_signal.item: Italy pushes to weaken EU green rules in €2 trillion budget framework; enforcement dilution extends fossil-fuel infrastructure lifetime and reduces clean-energy investment incentives.
carbon_policy_signal.why_it_matters: Weakened climate enforcement delays coal/gas phase-out, suppresses carbon price floor, and flattens merit-order transition to gas/renewables. Downside EUA price discovery if sectoral decarbonization targets erode.

freshness_caveat: Coal data is 195 days old (as of 2025-12-26) and Clean Dark is 190 days old (as of 2025-12-31); both stale. Coal 7th-percentile headline and Clean Dark 48th-percentile rank unreliable for current trading; use live forward curves and spreads instead. All other metrics current as of 2026-07-08/09.
risk_flags: Coal at 7th-percentile (USD 96/t, 195 days old) — thermal competitiveness minimal; any renewable weakness reverses hard.
Storage 50.88% full, 15.1pp below seasonal, 25th-percentile rank — summer refill shortfall risks autumn tightness and power curve inversion.
Russia refinery strikes + Iran sanctions remove ~2M b/d crude equivalent from global market; Brent support reduces LNG switching incentive, keeping TTF bid.
GB Power 91st-percentile (127.75 EUR/MWh) vs DE 79th (149.97 EUR/MWh) — 22 EUR/MWh spread; interconnector constraints amplify GB supply premium.

base.summary: Renewables stay elevated, storage refills slowly; TTF stable near 49, DE power drifts 145–155 EUR/MWh.

downside.summary: Russian LNG servicing loophole widens; Iranian crude re-enters via third-party cargoes; spot LNG floods EU, TTF slides on oversupply and storage refill relief.

upside.summary: Hormuz escalation or Russian LNG sanctions tightened; Brent +8-12%, TTF bid via LNG displacement and crude-gas arb compression.

themes: Renewables suppressing thermal dispatch; Clean Spark elevated
Geopolitical crude/LNG tightness via Russia/Iran; TTF supported
Storage 15pp below seasonal; refill pace critical for H2
GB-DE power premium widening on tight North Sea flows
top_drivers: Renewables at 92nd-percentile (68.87% of load) crush coal and gas merit order; Clean Spark at 92nd-percentile (39.62 EUR/MWh) reflects tight thermal dispatch window.
Geopolitical crude tightness (Russia refinery strikes, Iran sanctions, Middle East escalation) reduces LNG switching incentive and anchors TTF bid at 49.02 EUR/MWh (65th-percentile, +5.25% daily).
Storage 15pp below seasonal (50.88%, 25th-percentile) signals summer refill risk and H2 power curve inversion; any cold front or demand shock locks in autumn premium.
top_takeaway: Renewables at 92nd-percentile suppress thermal merit order; Clean Spark at 92nd-percentile and GB Power at 91st-percentile signal tight supply. Geopolitical crude/LNG tightness (Russia refinery strikes, Iran sanctions, Middle East escalation) underpins TTF upside.

watchlist.metric: EU sanctions on Russian LNG fleet servicing
watchlist.why: Implementation date and scope determine near-term Russian export capacity; direct TTF floor/ceiling depending on compliance enforcement.

watchlist.metric: Hormuz Strait disruption risk (Middle East escalation)
watchlist.why: Crude risk premium and LNG feedstock competition signal TTF +5-12% upside in tail scenarios; watch insurance and tanker premiums.
At 50.88% and 15pp below seasonal, summer refill pace sets H2 power price floor and fuel-switch trigger; 12pp gap closes or H2 tightness accelerates.

watchlist.metric: GB interconnector flows and North Sea maintenance
watchlist.why: GB-DE 22 EUR/MWh premium unsustainable if flows normalize; any outage extends GB premium and props up DA prices.
